images.title: Base 4, arcs 5 and 6
images.purpose: Show the construction of a triangle with sides 4, 5 and 6 using a base and two arcs.
images.composition: Base AB low and central, arcs above it meeting at C, white space around.
exact_structure: A horizontal teal (#0072B2) segment AB labelled 4 cm, with dots at A (left) and B (right).
An amber (#E69F00) arc centred at A of radius 5 cm on the upper side.

A reddish purple (#CC79A7) arc centred at B of radius 6 cm on the upper side, crossing the amber arc at exactly one point above AB; C is only a little to the right of A (about 0.6 cm), so the triangle leans to the left and is tall.
The crossing point has a dot and the label C.
Thin grey (#6B7280) segments AC labelled 5 cm and BC labelled 6 cm complete the triangle.
rejection: arc radii not matching 5 cm from A and 6 cm from B
more than one crossing point above AB
any side label other than 4 cm, 5 cm, 6 cm
any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: Draw the base, then an arc of one length from each end: the crossing is the third corner.
images.description: Base AB of 4 cm with a 5 cm arc from A and a 6 cm arc from B crossing at C.
images.context: Shown beside the concept text and video for this concept.
images.teaching_notes: Read the three lengths off the figure and say which arc comes from which end.

image_decisions.why: The method concept is clearest as the finished construction diagram with arcs and labelled lengths.
